description: Wikimpacts 1.0 is a global climate impact database built by automated information extraction from Wikipedia, giving quantitative estimates of the human and economic consequences of climate-related hazard events. Each event record carries minimum and maximum values with an approximate flag for eight impact dimensions: deaths, affected persons, displaced, homeless, injuries, buildings damaged, economic damage and insured damage, with the currency and inflation reference year for damages; events affecting several countries or places list all administrative areas. It is a joint initiative of the Swedish Centre for Impacts of Climate Extremes (Uppsala University and Research Institutes of Sweden), the Department of Water and Climate at the Vrije Universiteit Brussel and the Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research, with the static version hosted by the Bolin Centre for Climate Research, and is described by Li and co-authors in Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences in 2026. A subset is published on the Humanitarian Data Exchange as a downloadable CSV of impact events plus a SQLite database, under a CC BY-NC licence, with event dates reaching back to the eleventh century and up to 2026. Caveats: values depend on what Wikipedia reports and on automated extraction, so ranges and flags should be respected, and the HDX copy is a subset. It is useful for historical event analysis, validating hazard exposure and impact models, and resilience benchmarking; a related record is the IDMC displacement database.
